clue.text: Irish army unit with French 4 that 26

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
the answer to 4 is a devil, and the French for devil is diable

explanation.surface: A soldier from an Irish regiment teams up with a French devil in a hopeless situation.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 4 is DEUCE, an old word for the devil; 'French 4' therefore asks for the French word for devil. 'with' is just a link, and 'that 26' reads as 'that can't be helped'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irremediable cannot be put right or cured, exactly a thing that can't be helped.

clue.text: What happens if my opponent's queen is en prise, presumably

definitions.text: What happens if my opponent's queen is en prise
definitions.meaning: a chess piece en prise is left open to capture, so the natural reply is to announce you will capture it
used as a phrase meaning 'I assume so' or 'I suppose'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the chess player's capture of an exposed piece and a casual way of saying one supposes something.

clue.text: Islander, formerly African, losing points

indicators.note: losing tells us some letters drop out of the longer word

parts.note: a Rhodesian was a citizen of the former African state of Rhodesia, now Zimbabwe
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Someone who used to be African has now lost their bearings on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E and S from RHODESIAN to leave the word for a native of the Greek island of Rhodes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rhodian is a native of Rhodes, so an islander from the Dodecanese.

clue.text: Old priest or inmate has to improve

indicators.note: has means the prisoner word contains the other pieces within it

parts.note: a fellow inmate is a mate, the word read here as the 'mate' inside 'inmate'
Eli was the elderly priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric or a prisoner must better himself.
explanation.walkthrough: MATE opens up to hold ELI and OR: M + ELI + OR + ATE. 'to' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To meliorate is a formal verb for making something better, a synonym of improve.

clue.text: Nick 2

definitions.meaning: Old Nick is a name for the devil
a two in cards or dice

explanation.definitionFit: Deuce is an old word for the devil (Old Nick) and also the two in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Old doctor topped by Tory in French town

indicators.note: topped means the head letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: Galen was the famous Greek physician of the ancient world
CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: An ancient physician is beheaded by a Conservative in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes G from GALEN to leave ALEN; 'by' places CON beside it, and 'in' links to the definition. Alençon in Normandy is famous for lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Alençon is a town in Normandy, northern France, known for its lace.

clue.text: Young film actor's plays to alter

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters frolic about and settle into a new order

explanation.surface: A film star's theatrical work is meant to change things.
explanation.walkthrough: Loretta Young was a Hollywood star; 'Young' poses as an adjective but is her surname. The 's reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Loretta Young was an Oscar-winning American film actress, so her first name completes the description.

clue.text: Tonic covered by dominant gives protection on Tyneside

indicators.note: covered by means one note name sits inside the other

parts.note: in tonic sol-fa the dominant, fifth note of the scale, is soh
ut is the old name for the tonic note, now called doh
shields as a verb means gives protection

explanation.surface: A drink of tonic with a strong head offers some shelter in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: These are musical terms, not a drink: in sol-fa, the tonic was once called ut and the dominant is soh. South Shields is a port at the mouth of the Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: South Shields is a coastal town at the mouth of the River Tyne, part of the Tyneside conurbation.

clue.text: Where honoured names are having a good run

definitions.meaning: names of the honoured are inscribed ... of honour
an idiom for enjoying a streak of success

explanation.definitionFit: Names of the honoured appear on a roll, and the idiom for a winning streak uses the same words.

clue.text: Find you near the majority

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
taken as written

indicators.note: the majority of a word is most of its letters, here all but the last

explanation.surface: Locate you close to most of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or discover it, a synonym of find.

clue.text: Tough about border — has to plant on roadside

indicators.note: about means the first word wraps around the others

parts.note: hard means tough
an edge is a border
must means has to

explanation.surface: A hardy hedge-trimmer is obliged to put a plant by the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' splits open around the other two pieces. Hedge mustard is a wild plant of the cabbage family.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedge mustard is a common wild plant of the cabbage family, often found along roadsides and waste ground.

clue.text: Three seen in Italian city

parts.note: tre is the Italian for three
viso is an old poetic Italian past participle of vedere, to see, meaning seen

explanation.surface: Three people are spotted in a city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Italian' tells us both pieces are Italian words.
explanation.definitionFit: Treviso is a city in the Veneto region of north-east Italy.

clue.text: Number coming in went out far from numb

indicators.note: coming in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: exited means went out
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number

explanation.surface: A hundred people came in as others left, and the mood was lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' and 'numb' sit side by side to misdirect.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited means stirred up and full of feeling, the opposite of numb.

clue.text: 4 took a chair if old

parts.note: sat means took a chair
an is an archaic word for if

explanation.surface: Someone sat down, if that is an old way of putting it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 4 is DEUCE, the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the Devil, and deuce is an old euphemism for the devil.

clue.text: Saw about leaders getting time after 4

indicators.note: about means the proverb word is wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, an adage
the van is the leading part of an army or movement

explanation.surface: A cutting tool goes round the front runners, who get extra time after a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' joins VAN and T. In tennis, the point after deuce (4) is advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the player who wins the point after deuce has advantage.

clue.text: Naiveté in forming capital

indicators.note: forming means the letters are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: Innocence plays a part in shaping a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vientiane is the capital city of Laos.

clue.text: Petition to put seed into the ground, say

indicators.note: say means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to inter is to put into the ground, so this is 'inter seed'

explanation.surface: A request to plant some seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to plead or petition on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Piece of one with fur in new coat

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
new means the letters are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: a cat is a furry animal

explanation.surface: Part of a fur animal is put inside a new coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns the coat into TOCA, and the furry animal goes into it after the first three letters. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a piece of keyboard music showing off the player's touch.

clue.text: Think what glasses can do

definitions.meaning: mirrors (looking-glasses) throw back light and images

explanation.definitionFit: To reflect means to ponder, and mirrors reflect images back.

clue.text: Holy man had us reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new shape

explanation.surface: A holy man got us to change our ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu holy man or ascetic.

clue.text: Get going with outstanding male follower

parts.note: star as an adjective means outstanding
a tup is a ram, a male sheep, and sheep are proverbial followers

explanation.surface: Start a business with an exceptional man who will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To start up is to get going, as with an engine or a business.

clue.text: Swell performed, holding catches when raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole thing is read upwards
holding means one word is placed within the other

parts.note: did means performed
nets means catches

explanation.surface: A swelling appeared on a performer who held catches high.
explanation.walkthrough: DID holding NETS gives DNETSID, which 'when raised' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or bulge outward.

clue.text: Free, they say, provided Queen takes 4

indicators.note: they say means we hear the words spoken rather than written

parts.note: loose means free
if means provided
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A free queen takes the devil, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: The devil's name is said LOO-si-fer, so its first syllables sound like the word for free. 'takes' is a link. The answer to 4 is DEUCE, the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is a name for Satan, and deuce is an old euphemism for the devil.

clue.text: Frost, say, checked for 18, say

annotationWithheld.why: Frost, say, checked for 18, say (5): Frost, say = RIME, sounding like RHYME, but no sound parse found for 'checked for 18' (18 = REFLECT)

clue.text: Poles in characteristic passage

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people have a characteristic way of travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A transit is a passage, the act of passing across or through.

clue.text: Retired priest comes in to put an end to bondage

indicators.note: comes in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: to slay is to kill or put an end to

indicators.note: retired means going backwards, the piece read in reverse

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a priest

explanation.surface: A retired cleric steps in to end servitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns REV to VER, which goes into SLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavery is the state of being held in bondage.

clue.text: Banter with a twisted edentate

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Some joking with a warped toothless animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Edentates are mammals with few or no teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The antbear (aardvark) is often classed with the edentates, toothless mammals.

clue.text: Is beyond the reach of social services, which is inevitable

definitions.text: Is beyond the reach of social services
definitions.meaning: someone that no help can reach
a phrase for something that must be accepted

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both that no one can assist and that something is unavoidable.
